A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DECO research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete Appendices A–B are readable and support reliable comparison, including the additional material in v3.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix B report original real-robot success counts across four manipulation tasks, including tactile-fusion ablations and out-of-distribution sorting tests.

after.justification: v3 retains the original robot evaluations and adds conditioning-pathway and vision-encoder experiments with reported success counts.

M1.justification: The proposed two-stage DECO procedure, modality-specific conditioning, tactile adapter, LoRA adaptation, and Equations (1)–(4) remain unchanged. v3 supplies additional component specifications; the permuted pathways and ResNet-18 models are experimental controls rather than replacements for the proposed architecture.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same DECO-50 tasks, objects, and dataset statistics. The interference-fit assembly pair and out-of-distribution sorting objects already appear in v1. The new experiments reuse existing task coverage.

E2.justification: ACT, DP, DP.t, and the original DECO comparison variants are retained. v3 adds internal comparison variants: DECO.ds with permuted conditioning pathways in Table 7 and ResNet-18 counterparts in Tables 17–20.

E3.justification: v3 adds controlled model configurations: swapping proprioceptive and tactile conditioning pathways on two assembly pairs and using ResNet-18 for DECO and DECO.p across four tasks. The original training settings, preprocessing, metrics, and trial counts remain unchanged; the added architectural specifications are disclosures.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's fusion and adapter-training ablations, v3 tests whether the specific modality-to-pathway assignment matters (Table 7) and whether vision-encoder capacity explains performance (Appendix B.3, Tables 17–20). These substantially strengthen analysis of the central architectural rationale.

E5.justification: v1 reports success counts without uncertainty intervals. v3 systematically adds Wilson 95% confidence intervals to aggregate task and stage results in Appendix B.2 and the encoder comparisons. Existing trial counts are retained; no increase in training repetitions or seed counts is documented.

E6.justification: New results include 0/40 final-stage successes for permuted DECO.ds versus 29/40 for standard DECO.ds, plus four-task encoder comparisons, such as DECO achieving 111/120 with ResNet-18 versus 103/120 with ResNet-34 on pick-and-place. These are additional configuration results. v3 also corrects Table 2's DECO.p 00081-s-2x entry from 16/20 to 17/20 and Table 4's assembly total from 55/100 to 55/80, matching existing appendix counts. Table 1's headline results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The conditional action formulation and Equations (1)–(4) are retained, with no added theorems, assumptions, derivations, or proofs. Explicit 28-dimensional state/action notation and network specifications clarify the existing formulation.

C1.justification: The abstract's numerical claims and three principal contributions remain unchanged. However, the conclusion removes v1's assertion that the adapter can be incorporated into any pretrained vision-based policy and instead presents broader VLA and hardware validation as future work.

C2.justification: v3 adds explanations linking pathway permutation to jitter and inadequate tactile conditioning, and interprets the encoder control as evidence against encoder capacity explaining the gains. It also explicitly acknowledges single-platform evaluation and normal-force-only sensing. The original task-dependent interpretation of tactile benefits is retained.

D1.justification: v3 adds important implementation specifications, including six 512-dimensional transformer blocks, MLP activations, tactile feature and gate dimensions, LoRA rank 32, and per-pad tactile layouts. It also supplies explicit code, project, and dataset links absent from v1. These substantially expand reproducibility information without establishing that the original implementation changed.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds tactile-representation references by Fu, Gao, Kerr, and Yang, and explicitly distinguishes DECO from Higuera et al.'s larger ControlNet-based adapter and pretraining requirements. Other research positioning largely remains intact; the Open X-Embodiment citation update refers to the same work.

P1.justification: Most prose and section organization are retained. Local revisions expand related work, clarify method descriptions, shorten the parameter-efficiency discussion, and revise limitations. v3 also adds Appendix B.3, acknowledgements, resource links, and updated affiliation and publication information.

P2.justification: v3 adds six tables covering pathway assignment, tactile-pad layout, and encoder comparisons. Existing appendix result tables gain confidence-interval lines and best-value emphasis. The original eight figures retain their content, with resizing or repositioning and an expanded Figure 6 caption.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens support for the architectural claims by addressing v1's unmatched vision encoders and untested pathway assignment through new controls. Confidence intervals, implementation specifications, access links, and narrower applicability claims improve assessability and reproducibility. Waste Disposal inconsistencies between Table 3 and Appendix B.2 remain, but the added controls and transparency provide a substantial net quality gain.
